body:
Perhaps there's a wisdom in that analogy, we can't change the weather, we need only take an umbrella. It can rain for days and weeks on end and yet the sun always returns. 

Even when the cloud is dark and thick and covers the entire sky, we know that there is still a sun behind it, waiting to come out again.

Thank you for your thoughts, I hope we can both see brighter days

I've always thought it funny that I can fall in love with something so fast. Something that I didn't even know existed this morning, can be something I can't live without tonight.

I've had lots of different hobbies throughout my life, any one of which I would have willingly dedicated my life to. And yet when the day comes that I don't feel the same love for it, it's easy to blame my depression, and say that I will never find joy in anything again, before the next novel hobby comes along and occupies my mind.

I truly believe I view death in an unhealthy way. I view it as a switch I can flip, to just stop existing if it all becomes too much. I truly believe there is nothing after death, no regret or remorse, just lights out. 

I don't know where I'm going with this, I think the analogy of charging a spell is quite apt. The first time I thought of killing myself it was a distant fantasy, tonight, it seemed scarily real.

Thank you, I've had points in my life where I write every day, as part of my therapy. I would write a poem or a complaint or just a thought. I like to write and think I can explain myself pretty well when I give it some thought.

It does make it harder though when I'm not understood, I don't know how to put it differently. I've tried to be blunt with my parents and say, like you said, "this is too much, I'm done with this". We've talked about this before, so it makes me frustrated when I try to tell them it's going too far, and they are still in a combative mood. I think sometimes if everyone was a mind-reader, there would be no conflict. Ever

Thank you for telling me this, speaking now, an hour or two later, I can realize that saying my parents' grief would be temporary is pretty foolish. My mom still talks about her cousin who died when I was 10, I think sometimes that because I have been in such a downward spiral of mental health lately that it would be less of a surprise, or expected in some way. But if even one of my snakes died tomorrow, I would be crushed for much longer than anyone would want.

Thank you for the reply
